issues.title: [RX 5700 XT / Navi 10] AMDGPU DM i2c OEM bus cannot complete any transfer — DC re-asserts the SDA pull-down on every open
issues.author: Yimura
issues.description:
## Disclosure: AI-assisted analysis, human-verified

This investigation made heavy use of AI assistance — cross-referencing kernel sources, triaging decompiler output, and drafting this report. Stating that up front because it should inform how you read it, not because it changes what is claimed.

Everything asserted here was verified against primary sources rather than taken on trust:

- **Code citations** are against v7.1.5 and every one is hyperlinked to the exact line, pinned to commit `155b42bec9cbb6b8cdc47dd9bd09503a81fbe493` — so the links cannot drift onto later code as the tree moves.
- **Register values** are direct readbacks from the hardware on my machine, not reconstructions.
- **The device's i2c line and address** were derived twice, independently: from this card's own VBIOS tables, and from reverse engineering Sapphire's TriXX.
- **Every hardware claim was reproduced on the machine and confirmed by me at the keyboard**, including the working userspace transfer.

Where something is inferred rather than observed, it is labelled as such — see the pre-2022 caveat under "Regression status". No logs, register values, commit hashes or code excerpts in this report are synthesized.

## Summary

On Navi 10, the DDC line exposed as `AMDGPU DM i2c OEM bus` cannot complete an i2c transfer to any address. Every transfer fails identically, and it fails **before the address phase** — so this is not a device-absent condition.

The cause is a read/write asymmetry in `hw_ddc.c`.

During a `suspend-then-hibernate` cycle, the TTM hibernation eviction path

resumes normally, but it leaves a `ttm_lru_bulk_move` list internally
inconsistent. Later (for me it was approx. 17 minutes), a routine `list_del` on that same list
tripped `BUG_ON` in `lib/list_debug.c:65` (`list_del corruption`), panicking the
kernel, which presents as a spontaneous reboot

issues.author: Maciej S. Szmigiero
issues.description:
From time to time I get a deadlock when hibernating a machine with amdgpu in `amdgpu_device_prepare()` -> `amdgpu_device_evict_resources()` -> `ttm_device_prepare_hibernation()` -> `ttm_tt_swapout()` -> `shmem_read_mapping_page_gfp()` -> `shmem_get_folio_gfp()` -> `shmem_alloc_and_add_folio()` -> `try_to_free_pages(`) -> `throttle_direct_reclaim()`.

And `throttle_direct_reclaim()` just waits forever for `kswapd` to make progress, which never happens so the machine is essentially deadlocked. 

Looking at the hibernation code it seems that the `prepare` callbacks 
happens *after* tasks are already frozen so no wonder `kswapd` will never make progress.

----

This was reproduced on the latest upstream kernel 7.1.3 but the current drm code does _not_ seem to have any material differences there.

Note this does NOT seem to be duplicate of #5470 since this does _not_ look like memory corruption, just deadlock with page reclaim code.

Also, this does not seem specific to particular type of a amdgpu GPU.

issues.title: [Navi 32] 256-entry identity GAMMA_LUT changes premultiplied overlay blending
issues.author: Stian
issues.description:
## Brief summary of the problem:

There is visible flickering in the COSMIC DE top panel when it switches between the GPU-composited path and an AMDGPU hardware overlay plane. With help from Codex, I traced it to an AMDGPU color-management issue: attaching an exact 256-entry identity GAMMA_LUT changes fractional premultiplied-alpha overlay blending.

This makes a translucent COSMIC panel lighter on a hardware overlay than when GPU-composited; clearing only `GAMMA_LUT` stops the flicker.

Expected: an identity LUT is equivalent to bypass.

Actual: the precomposited reference and equivalent overlay composition produce different CRCs.

![visual-comparison.png](/uploads/337db9072c98b75d51928dc225dee1f9/visual-comparison.png){width="900" height="377"}

`amdgpu_dm_color.c` states that a linear DGM/RGM LUT should put the hardware block into bypass. The driver classifies this LUT as linear, making `has_regamma=false`, but selects the legacy path solely from its 256-entry size. That path enables `cm_is_degamma_srgb` and changes the plane blend domain.

I tested this fix in an otherwise unchanged build of the exact distribution kernel source:

```diff
-	is_legacy = regamma_size == MAX_COLOR_LEGACY_LUT_ENTRIES;
+	is_legacy = has_regamma &&
+		    regamma_size == MAX_COLOR_LEGACY_LUT_ENTRIES;
```

Results:

- Stock: identity LUT confirmed attached; panel flickered; reduced IGT failed with CRC mismatch `0x2133 != 0xa3d1`.
- Patched: the same identity LUT was attached; no flicker; reduced

issues.description:
## Brief summary of the problem:

With high enough display bandwidth requirements to trigger SubVP or DRR SubVP reclocking, memory clock P-state changes (automatic or manual DPM) cause the desktop to stall for a few frames, causing a very visible short freeze, which is unlikely to be desired during reclocking.

This turns out to be a faulty hardware lock introduced in https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/agd5f/linux/-/commit/00c391102abc13763e2bfc90e05503109b19f074, later renamed in https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/agd5f/linux/-/commit/6d92c4d03063480a60bbc3ff61d22197c931f411.

Working around this lock by either removing it entirely or gating it behind a `dmub_hw_lock_mgr_does_context_require_lock` check works flawlessly and eliminates the stall completely: [fams2-mclk-stutter-workaround-minimal.patch](/uploads/09e73a73cacf4c580c8835aceaa574ee/fams2-mclk-stutter-workaround-minimal.patch). I tested this workaround on various different configurations (HDR, VRR, MPO, suspend/resume, hotplugs, etc.) and it never caused any issues. Perhaps it's not needed for dGPUs at all? Especially since without it, SubVP looks like it's doing the correct thing - hiding the clock switch perfectly without any hitches.

Other people report temporary screen blanking rather than stutter on a clock speed change, but it turns out that's due to DRR on some Samsung panels, which seem to blank on VRR on/off transitions. This can be worked around by always setting the `VRR_ENABLED` property to `1` on affected CRT

## Brief summary of the problem:

On an RX 9070 XT (Navi 48 / GFX1201 / DCN 4.0.1), my Samsung Odyssey G70NC connected via DisplayPort randomly loses signal for \~1 second every few minutes when running at high refresh rates with a second monitor connected. issues.title: amdgpu: BUG_ON in amdgpu_device_mm_access on re-probe of Navi 48 after VFIO passthrough
issues.author: Faruk Aydin
issues.description:
## Summary

Re-probing a Navi 48 (RX 9070 XT, 1002:7550) with amdgpu after the card has been used by a VM via vfio-pci hits:

```
kernel BUG at drivers/gpu/drm/amd/amdgpu/amdgpu_device.c:720!
```

which is

```c
BUG_ON(!IS_ALIGNED(pos, 4) || !IS_ALIGNED(size, 4));
```

in `amdgpu_device_mm_access()`, called from `amdgpu_discovery_init()` while reading the IP-discovery table out of VRAM. After a VM has run on the card, the discovery TMR location/size the driver computes from device state is garbage (unaligned), and the driver BUG()s instead of failing probe.

This worked on v7.0.12 (same card, same reclaim flow, dozens of cycles) and regressed by v7.1.2.

## Impact goes beyond the crash

The BUG kills the probing task mid-`really_probe()`. Since the driver core sets `dev->driver` and creates the sysfs driver link _before_ calling probe, the device is left as a zombie: `lspci -k` / sysfs claim "Kernel driver in use: amdgpu", but no DRM device exists (no `drm/` sysfs dir, no /dev/dri node) and probe's error path never ran. Any later interaction with

this half-bound device (including a subsequent unbind) operates on inconsistent state. Only a reboot recovers the GPU for host use.

Requested behavior: validate the discovery blob location/size read from the device and fail probe with an error (as other discovery-validation paths already do) instead of BUG_ON on device-provided data.

## Brief summary of the problem:

The VBIOS data of the AsRock BC-250 results in a nonzero `dprefclk_ss_percentage` (set via the VBIOS smu_info table's `gpuclk_ss_percentage` ) but the actual DisplayPort clock seems to remain at 6000.

The audio clock code applies spread spectrum correction to its clock and so there ends up being a mismatch.

DCCG_AUDIO_DTO1_MODULE gets configured to 598874 kHz, but CLK4_CLK2_CURRENT_CNT reads exactly 6000.

Therefore the audio, being configured with SS correction while the main DP clock is not, is slow by 7 seconds per hour.

When watching a movie the audio eventually no longer matches up with the visuals.

I have attached a kernel patch that fixes the issue on my system (by completely disabling SS correction for this chip) but I wanted to get more expert feedback here before submitting upstream.

issues.title: amdgpu: deferred drm .release clears pci drvdata owned by another driver (vfio-pci), NULL-deref on unbind/runtime-PM
issues.author: Faruk Aydin
issues.description:
## Summary

`amdgpu_driver_release_kms()` calls `pci_set_drvdata(adev->pdev, NULL)` (drivers/gpu/drm/amd/amdgpu/amdgpu_kms.c:1608 in v7.1.2). This function is the DRM `.release` callback, so it runs at the _final_ `drm_dev_put()` — which is deferred until the last userspace reference to the DRM device is dropped, not at unbind time.

In a GPU-passthrough workflow (unbind amdgpu -\> bind vfio-pci, standard VFIO practice), any process still holding the dGPU's DRM node open at unbind time (a GPU monitoring daemon such as LACT, a compositor, etc.) delays the final release past the point where vfio-pci has bound the device and stored its own drvdata. When the last DRM fd closes, amdgpu's deferred release then NULLs **vfio-pci's** drvdata.

Every subsequent vfio-pci path that dereferences drvdata crashes:

- `vfio_pci_remove` -\> `vfio_pci_core_unregister_device` -\> `vfio_pci_core_sriov_configure` (on unbind) — observed, oops attached
- `vfio_pci_core_runtime_suspend` (runtime PM) — observed on an earlier boot
- `vfio_pci_core_aer_err_detected` would equally be affected

A secondary effect makes this worse: the oopsed sysfs `unbind` write dies holding the device lock, so any later PCI operation on the device blocks in uninterruptible D-state. When libvirt is the caller (qemu hook), libvirtd deadlocks until reboot.
